facts.fact: In eMarketer's benchmarks, open-exchange streaming TV is the cheapest platform tier, at about $15 to $30 CPM (media only).
facts.quote: Open-exchange streaming is the cheapest TV advertising CPM by platform tier, at about $15 to $30 per thousand impressions in eMarketer’s benchmarks.

facts.fact: Per the page's summary of eMarketer benchmarks, direct premium streaming TV runs $25 to $65 CPM, live sports streaming runs $40 to $80 or more, and national linear broadcast runs $25 to $40 CPM.
facts.quote: Direct premium streaming runs $25 to $65, live sports streaming runs $40 to $80 or more, and national linear broadcast runs $25 to $40.

facts.fact: The page states that its TV CPM ranges are media-only market ranges from eMarketer's benchmarks, not rate cards.
facts.quote: These are media-only market ranges, pulled from eMarketer’s benchmarks, not rate cards.

facts.fact: Platform fees, data costs and creative costs are not included in the media CPM ranges and are charged on top.
facts.quote: Platform fees, data costs and creative cost extra.

facts.fact: CPM is defined as cost per thousand impressions, the price an advertiser pays for an ad to be shown 1,000 times.
facts.quote: CPM is cost per thousand impressions: the price an advertiser pays for an ad to be shown 1,000 times.

facts.fact: A 2026 roundup computed roughly $80 per 1,000 viewers for Super Bowl LX; this is a third-party cost-per-viewer calculation, not an impression-based CPM.
facts.quote: computed roughly $80 per 1,000 viewers for Super Bowl LX.

facts.fact: Digital Applied, citing IAB, projected US connected TV ad spend at $37.95 billion in 2026.
facts.quote: put US CTV ad spend at a projected $37.95 billion in 2026.

facts.fact: Digital Applied reported CTV upfront commitments of $17.73 billion were forecast to exceed primetime linear upfronts of $16.98 billion for the first time.
facts.quote: CTV upfront commitments ($17.73 billion) were forecast to exceed primetime linear upfronts ($16.98 billion) for the first time.

facts.fact: MoffettNathanson forecast that US linear core TV ad revenue would fall 7% to $55.2 billion in 2025, with local stations down 22%.
facts.quote: MoffettNathanson forecast that US linear core TV ad revenue would fall 7% to $55.2 billion in 2025, with local stations down 22%

facts.fact: The page has not found current, verified CPMs for individual services such as Netflix, Hulu, Disney+ or Peacock.
facts.quote: We have not found current, verified CPMs for individual services such as Netflix, Hulu, Disney+ or Peacock

facts.fact: Impression count is calculated by dividing the budget by the CPM and multiplying by 1,000.
facts.quote: divide the budget by the CPM and multiply by 1,000.

facts.fact: Adwave daily budgets start at $30.
facts.quote: On Adwave, [daily budgets start at $30](https://adwave.com/pricing/) and are paid from a prepaid wallet

facts.fact: Adwave daily budgets are paid from a prepaid wallet with no subscription or contract.
facts.quote: are paid from a prepaid wallet, with no subscription or contract

facts.fact: Adwave's daily budget is an all-in price covering media, ads, and management, with no fees added on top.
facts.quote: the daily budget is an all-in price covering media, ads, and management, with no fees added on top

facts.fact: On Adwave, TV, Google (YouTube, Demand Gen and Search), Facebook and Instagram are available from $30 a day.
facts.quote: TV, Google (YouTube, Demand Gen and Search), Facebook and Instagram are available from $30 a day

facts.fact: On Adwave, Reddit is available from about $35 a day.
facts.quote: and Reddit from about $35

facts.fact: Adwave does not guarantee a specific CPM or placement on a given service.
facts.quote: Adwave does not guarantee a specific CPM or placement on a given service.

facts.fact: Adwave's campaign creative is included in the campaign price, and extra creation is priced separately.
facts.quote: Campaign creative is included, and extra creation is priced separately.

facts.fact: The tier CPM ranges on the page are eMarketer market benchmarks reported for 2026 and were checked in October 2026, with scope limited to the US.
facts.quote: The tier ranges are eMarketer market benchmarks reported for 2026 and checked in October 2026. Scope is the US.

facts.fact: The benchmark rows on the page are not fully comparable: most are media CPMs, the Super Bowl LX figure is a computed cost per viewer, and open-exchange prices are auction-driven while premium and broadcast prices are mostly negotiated.
facts.quote: The rows are not fully comparable. Most are media CPMs, the Super Bowl LX figure is a computed cost per viewer, and open-exchange prices are auction-driven

facts.fact: Ad spend figures for CTV and linear on the page are forecasts, not actual spend, and describe the market rather than the price of a single buy.
facts.quote: Ad spend figures for CTV and linear are forecasts, labeled as such, and describe the market rather than the price of any single buy.

facts.fact: Per-service CPMs for Netflix, Hulu and others are not published in the sources the page checked, so none appear in its table.
facts.quote: Per-service CPMs for Netflix, Hulu and others are not published in the sources checked, so none appear in the table.

facts.fact: Viewing share is not ad inventory; a service with a large share of TV time may sell little of it to advertisers.
facts.quote: Viewing share is not ad inventory. A service that holds a large share of TV time may sell little of it to advertisers
